Phase 5c: Route B run and dead. MpiH3EncodeAV over source+extension (N=141, S=51, E=90 - all three forced by the 17k+5 video grid, the 3-frame audio step and the 17-frame latent step), mask over the extension only, MpiH3DecodeAV compositing back. Join 30.18 (5.56x) against the shipped one-frame pin's 2.02 (0.36x): 15x looser, and the driver changes clothes across the seam. THE MECHANISM IS NOT WHAT FAILED - F8 re-ran the same sample with the composite off (25s, ComfyUI cached the sampler) and its decoded head IS the source, so the noise mask reached the sampler and the preserved region survived every step. Composite eliminated (30.38 without it), VAE round trip eliminated (-0.83 luma over the head vs +12 at the join). H3 takes identity from the GUIDE, not from unmasked latent tokens, which makes Route B and Phase 1's MpiH3MaskedPrefix ONE mechanism rather than two. Correction: feather is a SPATIAL softener (max_pool2d+conv2d over H,W, h3.py:986-1010), a no-op on a full-frame mask and never a temporal crossfade. BLOCKED and needing Fabio's decision: MiniMaxH3AddGuide anchors a CLIP (17k+5, frame_idx in pixel frames), which is LTX's shape through the path H3 listens to, but three arms died in the sampler and a minimal-diff probe (the control with only #902 num_frames 1->39) died identically. custom_nodes/ComfyUI-MiniMax-H3-Extend/patch.py monkey-patches PackedLayout.__init__ and MiniMaxH3.extra_conds at import for EVERY graph on 8188: one frame's rows per image keyframe ([4860,96] into [405,96]) and 'only first/last keyframe anchors are supported'. Stock PackedLayout on CPU sizes 1/7/12 steps correctly. The bench is not the engine Vision ships.

Phase 5d: the clip guide runs, and the seam metric was rewarding the artefact. Pack renamed .disabled and the bench restarted; both previously impossible arms then ran first time unchanged, proving the [4860,96]->[405,96] layout failure and 'only first/last keyframe anchors' were the pack's patch. MiniMaxH3AddGuide now anchors the source's last 39 frames as a CLIP at frame_idx 0 with its matching audio tail, ref_audio_1 dropped. F10a discards the model's re-take and joins hard (LTX #44/#45) at 205.5s; F10b keeps it and linear_blends the original back over all 39 frames (LTX #43) at 5.0s cached. HEADLINE: join/source-half-mean never measured smoothness, it measured STILLNESS. The control's 2.02 is a DIP - 2.0 where its own neighbours run 4.6-6.6 and the footage's ordinary motion is 5.68 - i.e. the picture nearly stops for one frame, which is exactly the 'start frame from the last frame' artefact Fabio reported. The target is 1.0x, not 0. F10b's crossfade region measures min 3.90 / max 7.47 / mean 5.59 across frames 84-124 against pure-source 5.68, no spike. Identity holds through the fade and 2.3s past it (frames 84/95/105/115/124/180 all the same woman), which no earlier arm managed. This reframes Phase 5b's table - the control's 0.36x was never the bar to beat. A build bug was caught before the numbers were read: the crossfade arm must keep the re-take, not the trimmed tail, or it blends a 1.6s time offset at full opacity with every tensor valid. ComfyUI-Manager has no reboot endpoint on this build (both routes 404). Gate is Fabio's eyes.

Fabio's gate on Phase 5d: continuation, identity and AUDIO all pass on both clip-guide arms ('their continuation is really good... the sound is good, flawless') - the guide's own audio input killed the re-sung-music problem that ran through Phase 5. One defect remains: a short transition flicker, 1-5 frames, worse on F10b. Measured before handoff and it is NOT colour - chroma is flat across the join (U +0.84, V -0.2 over 20-frame windows). It is luma: the model's RE-TAKE of the guide is up to +4.9 brighter than the original, and linear_blend ramps that in monotonically across the overlap (F10b-F10a rises 0.0 -> +4.9 from frame 85 to 117), then frames 119-124 swing 3-6 luma and drop back to 103.6 at the first pure new frame. The model's CONTINUATION sits at the source's own level - only the re-take drifts, and the re-take is exactly what the crossfade mixes. F10a's version is a single -2.4 step, compounded by the source brightening 103.8->105.9 through the overlap while the continuation does not follow. Fix order: level-match the re-take before blending, then filmic/perceptual crossfade modes (both untested; linear_blend was chosen only because flow_ltx_extend.json uses it), then guide length 56/73. Do NOT widen the overlap - the excursion scales with it. BENCH: ComfyUI-MiniMax-H3-Extend stays renamed .disabled for this work.

Phase 5e: the transition flicker is fixed on the metric, and it was TWO defects wearing one name. Eight arms off ONE cached sample (5-10s each; everything changed sits downstream of #409). Defect 1 was the drifted re-take, diagnosed in 5d. Defect 2 was NEW: the model's first genuinely new frame (generated 39) is a one-frame flash at 106.6 against 103.5 for generated 40 on and 104.5 for the source beside it - and it sits at output frame 124, OUTSIDE the crossfade (overlap_side source blends source 85..123 against generated 0..38), so no overlap_mode and no re-take match could ever reach it. LEAD 2 IS DEAD ON BOTH MODES: filmic_crossfade 6.95/4.33 is WORSE than linear_blend's 6.68/4.23 and perceptual_crossfade 6.68/4.21 is identical to it - both reshape the weighting curve, neither touches the level being weighted. LEAD 1 WORKS AND COSTS NO REFERENCE NODE: #902 is GetImageRangeFromBatch(start_index -1, num_frames 39) and KJNodes resolves -1 to 'the last num_frames', so #902 already IS source frames 85..123; ColorMatch is per-frame across equal batches, and reinhard (mean/std) beats mkl on both arms it ran. DROPPING the flash frame is a trap the luma metric rewards - join motion runs 6.98 -> 8.75 -> 10.84 for 0/1/2 frames dropped, one artefact traded for a 42ms skip. F12k keeps it and level-matches it against its OWN SUCCESSOR (generated 40 already sits at the source's level): luma span 1.33, worst 1-frame step 1.10 against the source's own +-0.4 wobble, join motion 5.34 vs the footage's 5.69 = 0.94x. Six nodes on top of F10b. Instrument note: flash.py cannot see this defect at all - a smooth +5 luma ramp has small frame-to-frame diffs the whole way up - so luma.py reads ABSOLUTE signalstats YAVG per frame with the motion series alongside, which is what caught the drop-frame trade. The audio drop index must NOT follow the picture's when the flash frame is put back (#942 starts at G, not G+1); nothing fails if it is wrong, the sound just slides a frame. Gate is Fabio's eyes on F12k, then the port into flow_h3_extend.json.

Phase 5f: 5e's claim was too strong and the sound artefact is ours. Fabio on F12k/F10b: 'Both videos still have a colour flicker, just not as much as before, and there is also a sound artefact. Sounds like a light switch.' Frame-MEAN luma is flat on F12k (span 1.33) and the eye still sees the flicker - a frame mean cannot see a regional or chromatic swing, so 5e killed one contributor, not the defect. THE SOUND IS A 17ms DROPOUT (-47 to -64 dB, 555 samples) starting exactly where the source ends, identical in F10a/F10b/F12k so it predates 5e. ROOT-CAUSED BY ELIMINATION, each step a probe not a reading: the model's raw audio (F13_raw, #442 fed from #409/#404) runs -19..-28 dB straight through its frame 39 with no hole; the sliced tail on its own (F14_tail, AudioConcat bypassed) starts at -24.4 dB clean; core AudioConcat is a plain torch.cat; and the source FILE is 165333 samples, loud to its last sample. Cross-correlating the tail against the finished file puts tail[0] at output sample 165888, not 165333 - 555 late, exactly the hole. 165888 = 162 x 1024, a whole number of AAC frames: MpiLoadVideo._load_audio (video.py:156-189) decodes the mp4's AAC to WAV and the decoder emits its final PADDED frame, so the loader returns a soundtrack 555 samples LONGER than the picture it came with, ending in the encoder's zero padding. Silent and harmless at the end of a clip, which is why nothing caught it - but this Flow concatenates onto that tail, and the source is itself an AAC-saved H3 render, so it compounds on every extend of an extend. FIXED IN THE FLOW with an existing node and no code change: #950 MpiAudioRange(#906, fps #331, start 0, end -1) into #907 audio1 - it counts in FRAMES so it re-derives round(124/24*32000) = 165333 with nothing hard-coded. Verified on F15a/F15b: the 4ms envelope across the join goes -19/-48/-56/-60/-59 dB to -19/-24/-27/-28/-28 dB, worst sample step 0.052 against the file's own 99.99pct of 0.081. THE NODE IS STILL WRONG for every other caller - that is /mpi-nodes-sync plus a pin bump and it is Fabio's call. GOTCHAS: the bench arms are 864x480, NOT 1280x704 (the source is an 864x480 H3 render and #916 sizes off the loader), and Phase 5 part 2 already had a metric INVERT between bench and app resolution, so nothing here should be quoted at app resolution without re-running; MpiSaveVideo truncates audio to the PICTURE length, which is why F14's tail measured 134667 rather than the 136000 MpiAudioRange returned; and select=gte(n,N) returns an empty stream from these files where an accurate -ss after -i does not. THE FLICKER IS RE-OPENED: regional per-cell luma at the join (4.64) sits inside the source's own range (4.60) and does not convict; chroma dU at frame 124 steps -0.97 against the source's +-0.19, about 5x, and is the standing lead; detail falls 1.04x -> 0.54x through the overlap and STAYS at 0.59x after, which is the continuation being softer, not an oscillation. F15b joins HARD with no crossfade anywhere and exonerates or convicts the fade in one watch; both arms are with Fabio.

Fabio's verdict on F15, and it separates two things in one watch. (1) THE PICTURE CROSSFADE IS CONVICTED: 'On F15B, it's barely noticeable, but the audio artefact is still there' and 'F-15A, the colour flicker is more apparent. And it also has the audio artefact.' F15a is the 39-frame linear_blend, F15b is a hard join with no crossfade anywhere - so the fade CAUSES most of the flicker rather than merely needing level-matching. That fade was carried over from flow_ltx_extend.json and is the wrong mechanism for H3; the hard join is the base from here, and Phase 5e's filmic/perceptual sweep was a sweep inside a fade that should not exist. The level-match still earns its place because the flash frame is on the hard arm too. On F15b the chroma lead is RETIRED - dU -0.08 / dV -0.03 at the join, flat, against the fading arm's -0.97 - and what remains is a two-frame luma decline of -2.35 at frames 123-124, because the source brightens 103.8 -> 105.5 through its last 40 frames and the model's continuation does not follow that trend. (2) THE AUDIO ARTEFACT IS NEITHER THE PICTURE STITCH NOR THE AAC HOLE: it survives both arms, and a whole-file scan of F15b finds nothing below -12 dB of its local median except the AAC priming at 0.000-0.025 s that the source clip has too. So the 17 ms hole was real, is fixed, and was not what he was hearing. What is left is the SPLICE - #907 AudioConcat butt-joins two different recordings at one sample with no fade, while the picture faded over 39 frames. MpiNodes already knew: MpiAudioSplice's own tooltip reads 'A hard splice clicks, and a click is the one artefact an audio edit cannot hide.' The Flow never used that node. F16 fades the sound over the model's own re-take of the same moment (#951 MpiAudioRange giving tail + F frames of re-take, #952 MpiAudioSplice with a NEGATIVE start so no source length is hard-coded and the patch lands flush with the end, which is the condition the node raises on). DO NOT CHASE the 4.7553 s single-sample step: the SOURCE clip has it at 1.8x its own 99.99th percentile, so it is content, not something the Flow introduced.

F16 built and run: #951 MpiAudioRange + #952 MpiAudioSplice crossfade the audio splice on the hard-joined picture, at 300ms (12-frame pre-roll) and 800ms (24-frame). F16a cost a full 205.3s because another job on the bench evicted the sample from ComfyUI's cache; F16b then cached at 5.0s. THE METRIC BARELY MOVES: worst sample step within +-40ms of the join goes 0.04872 (0.60x the file's own 99.99th pct) hard, to 0.04181 (0.65x) at 300ms and 0.04057 (0.65x) at 800ms. The splice was never a large step - it is quieter than the music's ordinary transients - so a fade can only move it a little. Both readings are live: if the fade fixes what Fabio hears then the step metric is simply the wrong instrument for a content discontinuity between two recordings; if it does not, the splice is exonerated and the remaining candidate is that the sound is already in the SOURCE clip, whose own biggest step sits at 4.7553s (frame 114) at 1.8x its own 99.99th percentile - 0.4s before the transition, close enough to read as being at it. The untouched source clip was sent to Fabio on its own to settle that, because no measurement here can tell a percussive transient in the music from an artefact.

Fabio's gate on F16: F16b PASSES CLEAN - 'F-16A still has a little flicker, almost imperceptible, and the sound is good. F-16B is perfect, both sound and image, no flicker at all.' THE HEADLINE: F16a and F16b have BIT-IDENTICAL VIDEO (ffmpeg -map 0:v -f md5 returns e56a0cd65c540e57bf2bd3fac81b67cf for both) and differ ONLY in the audio crossfade - 300ms over a 12-frame pre-roll vs 800ms over 24. So the 'little flicker' on F16a was not in the pixels at all: the audio splice was being perceived as a VISUAL event at the transition, which is exactly why every picture-side instrument kept measuring flat while the eye kept objecting. That also retires the residual two-frame luma decline of -2.35 as something to chase - it is in both arms byte for byte and invisible once the sound is right. THE WINNING CONFIG is four changes, each with its own evidence: (1) MiniMaxH3AddGuide anchors the source's last 39 frames as a CLIP with its own audio and ref_audio_1 dropped; (2) HARD JOIN - #904 overlap 1, the model's re-take discarded, NO 39-frame crossfade; (3) ColorMatch/reinhard on the model's first free frame against its own successor; (4) #950 MpiAudioRange(#906, 0, -1) trimming the AAC padding plus #951/#952 MpiAudioSplice crossfading the splice over 24 frames / 800ms. REPRODUCIBILITY GOTCHA found by the same md5: F15b and F16a share a seed, a prompt and an upstream graph yet their video md5s differ (8d4baf30 vs e56a0cd6), because F16a re-sampled from scratch after another job evicted ComfyUI's cache and F16b then reused F16a's sample. The bench is NOT bit-reproducible across a cache eviction, so any A/B spanning one compares two samples rather than two stitches - check the video md5 before attributing a difference to the change under test. NEXT: port F16b into comfy_workflows/flow_h3_extend.json and its raw/ twin.

Phase 5h - the 8-step alignment. MPI-687's c39b5008 swapped flow_h3_extend onto the 8-step distill for dependency reasons and explicitly did not re-tune it, leaving an 8-step LoRA sampled the 4-step way. The sampler arm now matches minimax_h3_r2va line for line, proved by arm_equivalence.py comparing the two graphs by shape: MpiLoraModel SWITCHED in/out at strength 1 instead of MpiLoraModelClip faded to 0.2, beta/8 instead of beta/6, sigma shift 12/4 turbo and 12/2 quality, Input_Refs.clip straight off the CLIPLoader. #457 and #915 deleted; 52 -> 53 nodes. THREE PRE-EXISTING DEFECTS FIXED on the branch being rebuilt: the quality arm had NO sigma shift at all, the turbo LoRA was applied to the CLIP and still at 0.2 when turbo was off, and #909 EasyCache hung off the raw UNET so the quality arm silently skipped ModelAttentionBackend. A V3 TRAP: the first run wrote steps 8 into BasicScheduler.scheduler because this engine declares a COMBO as the literal string 'COMBO' rather than as the list of options, and a missed COMBO consumes no positional slot so every LATER widget shifts by one - verify-workflow, the injection validator and 883 tests all pass on that graph, and ONLY the raw round trip caught it. PROOFS: round trip 0 differences, check 3 graphToPrompt 0 differences, verify-workflow and validate-injection-rules green AGAINST 48188 (the engine was up this session, closing Phase 5g's deviation), npm test 883/883. PIN BLOCKER CLEARED: MpiNodes 1.2.9 e00086a9 is pinned and carries MpiAudioSplice. THE GATE IS UNRUN AND DELIBERATELY SO: no generation was dispatched because Fabio was mid-test on the GPU with no lease and asked for it to be left alone, so F16b's pass and every Phase 5d-5g number including the e56a0cd6 md5 are 4-step evidence that no longer describes this graph. Remaining: one bench run with the Phase 5g inputs, luma.py + dropouts.py, and Fabio watching an 8-step extend. The two-pass sweep is MPI-688, not this card.
